prereg_rule: "A beats B" = A has a strictly lower ED_U in at least ceil(2/3 of the units) (5 of 7; 4 of 6) AND a lower mean ED_U over the units, against every listed B.

A_per_unit_check.forecast_per_unit: single deterministic run per origin (no reps in confirm.json)

C_secondary.note: Secondary metrics as listed in the prereg ('reported, not used for the verdict'). The 5/7, 4/6 rule is applied to them ONLY descriptively, to see whether they tell the same story as the primary.

forecast_pcc.note: pcc = PCC over genes of predicted vs true mean change from stage s (higher is better). persist is NaN by construction (zero predicted change); uot_rw / tilt_rw are NaN where rolling origin chose lambda 0 (the forecast IS persist). So pcc cannot rank uot_rw vs persist at all, and vs meanshift / tilt_rw only where both are defined.

forecast_ess.note: ESS = 1 / sum w^2 of the scored (subsampled) weights; 1500 = unweighted. Not a competition metric: it measures how hard the reweighting is.

exploratory.note: EXPLORATORY, not pre-registered. Nothing here alters the pre-registered verdict; only a real bug in the frozen pipeline would matter, and that would need a new pre-registered run.

H2_tie_structure.note: Where rolling origin picked lambda 0 the uot_rw forecast is the persist forecast (identical arrays, exact float equality, a tie under 'strictly lower'). This is part of the frozen method (lambda 0 is in the grid), not a reason to relax the rule.

H1c_meaningfulness.construction: indep = midpoint 0.5 x + 0.5 y of INDEPENDENT draws: covariance 0.25 S_A + 0.25 S_B (half of the average within-stage covariance), mean 0.5 mu_A + 0.5 mu_B. Every balanced method (union, indep, ot_pairs, sb_half) has the same mean (interp_bench_frozen header), so ot_pairs vs indep differs only in shape / spread: H1c tests the quality of the pairing given displacement interpolation, not whether interpolating beats the 50/50 mixture.

rep_spread.caveat: Reps are PAIRED: the held-stage target subsample is the same (seed 1) in every rep; only the fit-side subsamples (seeds 1000+r, 2000+r) and the pair / mixture draws (rng 1000k+r) change. So the rep sd measures fit-side sampling noise only, not target-side or embryo-level variation, and with n = 3 the sd itself is very noisy. Per-pool differences (secondary.pool_ED_U) are the closer proxy for embryo-level variation.
